repo.name: native
repo.description: Dart packages related to native interop and the foreign function interface. Contains code generators for generating bindings for other programming languages and packages related to the hooks system for bundling native code,

issue.title: [ffigen] Use `objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue`
issue.body_html:
From the documentation, I think we can just replace all our calls to objc_retain with this function. If the reference was not recently autoreleased, this is the same as an objc_retain call. But if it was autoreleased, then this essentially promotes the autoreleased reference to a strong reference.

This would reduce the number of autoreleased references we hold, helping to mitigate dart-lang/sdk#61129 / #3652 (though it's still not a complete solution, because the ObjC APIs the user is calling could autorelease their own internal references).

Thanks for the tip @brianquinlan

issue.body:
From the [documentation](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/AutomaticReferenceCounting.html#arc-runtime-objc-retainautoreleasedreturnvalue), I *think* we can just replace all our calls to `objc_retain` with this function. If the reference was not recently autoreleased, this is the same as an `objc_retain` call. But if it was autoreleased, then this essentially promotes the autoreleased reference to a strong reference.

This would reduce the number of autoreleased references we hold, helping to mitigate https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/61129 / https://github.com/dart-lang/native/issues/3652 (though it's still not a complete solution, because the ObjC APIs the user is calling could autorelease their own internal references).

Thanks for the tip @brianquinlan

comments.body_html:
I actually did an experiment with this and I don't think that it always works (#3652).

The problem is that some APIs calls (e.g. NSURLSession.dataTaskWithRequest) seem to add things to the autorelease pool other than their return values. After you call NSURLSession.dataTaskWithRequest, you'll see that the 7 objects in the autorelease pool (instead of the expected one). Those objects include __NSCFLocalDataTask and __CFN_TaskMetrics (whatever those are).

From the documentation, I think we can just replace all our calls to objc_retain with this function.
...
But I think this still worth doing, as long as objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue is actually a drop-in replacement for objc_retain.

It's not so simple as just calling objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue: There is a special protocol between caller and callee.

The called ObjC function that returns the object will get the return address from the stack and look at the following machine instructions to see if it fits a certain pattern (see here). This is also described e.g. here

So we cannot just use a FFI calls to objc_msgSend and then another FFI call to objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue with the returned value -- it will not take it out of autorelease pool.

comments.body_html:
The called ObjC function that returns the object will get the return address from the stack and look at the following machine instructions to see if it fits a certain pattern (see here). This is also described e.g. here

FWIW, when I was experimenting with this, I created one Objective-C trampoline per bound method so clang would be responsible for generating the correct code. But I thought that this wasn't worth it because:

  1. it's a lot of extra native code generation
  2. it doesn't actually fix the problem (because some methods add to the autorelease pool as an implementation detail)

The trampoline looks like:

__attribute__((ns_returns_retained))
NSURLSessionDataTask* URLSession_dataTaskWithRequest(NSURLSession* session,
                                                    NSURLRequest* request) {
  return [session dataTaskWithRequest:request];
}

The generated code ends with:

blr  x8                    ; calls objc_msgSend
mov  x29, x29              ; <-- the magic marker instruction for arm64
bl   0x78                  ; calls objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue

You can then change the generated binding like:

      final $ret = <call trampoline>
-    return NSURLSessionDataTask.fromPointer($ret, retain: true, release: true);
+    // Don't retain because the trampoline has already incremented the reference count.
+    return NSURLSessionDataTask.fromPointer($ret, retain: false, release: true);

comments.body_html:
The landed PR does not actually do anything because there is a protocol between objc_autoreleaseReturnValue and objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue which you need to follow for hand-off to succeed.

See the code, more specifically prepareOptimizedReturn and acceptOptimizedReturn.

TLDR is that on ARM64 objc_autoreleaseReturnValue will put a tuple of (obj, return-address) into the TLS and objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue will check whether return-address corresponds to its call-site. There are also some corner-cases (e.g. classes which intercept retain / release messages are handled specially) where these methods will look at instructions at the call-site to detect a special marking instructions (e.g. mov fp, fp on ARM64).

I don't think we can fully satisfy the protocol without some low-level surgery in the FFI implementation in the VM.

PS. Additional data point. If you take the PR and revert all the changes except changes in the tests - those tests will still pass. Which seems to indicate that the PR does not do anything.

comments.body:
The landed PR does not actually do anything because there is a protocol between `objc_autoreleaseReturnValue` and `objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue` which you need to follow for hand-off to succeed. 

See [the code](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/objc4/blob/fb265098298302243cd7eeaa1f63f0ba7786dd9a/runtime/NSObject.mm#L2335-L2342), more specifically [`prepareOptimizedReturn`](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/objc4/blob/fb265098298302243cd7eeaa1f63f0ba7786dd9a/runtime/objc-object.h#L1612-L1673) and [`acceptOptimizedReturn`](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/objc4/blob/fb265098298302243cd7eeaa1f63f0ba7786dd9a/runtime/objc-object.h#L1676-L1724).

TLDR is that on ARM64  `objc_autoreleaseReturnValue` will put a tuple of `(obj, return-address)` into the TLS and `objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue` will check whether `return-address` corresponds to its call-site. There are also some corner-cases (e.g. classes which intercept `retain` / `release` messages are handled specially) where these methods will look at instructions at the call-site to detect a special marking instructions (e.g. `mov fp, fp` on ARM64). 

I don't think we can fully satisfy the protocol without some low-level surgery in the FFI implementation in the VM.  

PS. Additional data point. If you take the PR and revert all the changes except changes in the tests - those tests will still pass. Which seems to indicate that the PR does not do anything.

comments.body_html:
Ok, that's a much bigger change then. We'd need to add a new flag similar to isLeaf to @Native etc, and then change the trampoline based on that flag. We would only really need to enable that flag for objc_msgSend and co (and only if they return an object pointer with a +0 reference).

As for how we change the trampoline:

  • The straightforward option would be to call objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue inside the trampoline, which is fine as long as the caller knows that this means the reference is now +1 instead of +0, and must be caught in a Dart wrapper object. As long as we're careful about version skew between VM/FFIgen/package:objective_c, this should be ok. A bit risky tho.
  • A fancier approach would be to try to make the objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue work by making the trampoline transparent, so that from Dart code it looks like we are directly calling objc_msgSend. This seems like it would be extremely difficult.

Overall I'm not sure it's worth it. Better to just wrap every objc_msgSend call in an autorelease pool. Seems like a lot of effort to go to to save a few ns.

See [the code](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/objc4/blob/fb265098298302243cd7eeaa1f63f0ba7786dd9a/runtime/NSObject.mm#L2335-L2342), more specifically [`prepareOptimizedReturn`](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/objc4/blob/fb265098298302243cd7eeaa1f63f0ba7786dd9a/runtime/objc-object.h#L1612-L1673) and [`acceptOptimizedReturn`](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/objc4/blob/fb265098298302243cd7eeaa1f63f0ba7786dd9a/runtime/objc-object.h#L1676-L1724).

TLDR is that on ARM64  `objc_autoreleaseReturnValue` will put a tuple of `(obj, return-address)` into the TLS and `objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue` will check whether `return-address` corresponds to its call-site. There are also some corner-cases (e.g. classes which intercept `retain` / `release` messages are handled specially) where these methods will look at instructions at the call-site to detect a special marking instructions (e.g. `mov fp, fp` on ARM64). 

I don't think we can fully satisfy the protocol without some low-level surgery in the FFI implementation in the VM.  

PS. Additional data point. If you take the PR and revert all the changes except changes in the tests - those tests will still pass. Which seems to indicate that the PR does not do anything.

timeline.body_html:
Ok, that's a much bigger change then. We'd need to add a new flag similar to isLeaf to @Native etc, and then change the trampoline based on that flag. We would only really need to enable that flag for objc_msgSend and co (and only if they return an object pointer with a +0 reference).

As for how we change the trampoline:

  • The straightforward option would be to call objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue inside the trampoline, which is fine as long as the caller knows that this means the reference is now +1 instead of +0, and must be caught in a Dart wrapper object. As long as we're careful about version skew between VM/FFIgen/package:objective_c, this should be ok. A bit risky tho.
  • A fancier approach would be to try to make the objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue work by making the trampoline transparent, so that from Dart code it looks like we are directly calling objc_msgSend. This seems like it would be extremely difficult.

Overall I'm not sure it's worth it. Better to just wrap every objc_msgSend call in an autorelease pool. Seems like a lot of effort to go to to save a few ns.

issue.body_html:
Flutter wraps every message loop task in an autorelease pool. We should do the same in Dart.

Without this, ObjC interop on background isolates is a prone to pseudo memory leaks. An ObjC object created on a background isolate may be kept alive by a thread-scoped autorelease pool, and live for a lot longer than it should.

This issue is affecting cupertino_http.

issue.title: Objective-C autorelease pools are never drained
issue.body_html:
I discovered this in the context of dart-lang/http#1791

With the recent fixes to package:objective_c and package:cupertino_http, package:cupertino_http still leaks 11,676 bytes/request when run on Dart or in an isolate on Flutter.

In Flutter, Objective-C autorelease pools are never drained on isolates other than the main isolate.
In Dart, Objective-C autorelease pools are never drained.

Repo (generated by AI but it is reasonable):

import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:isolate';

import 'package:objective_c/objective_c.dart';

const batches = 8;
const perBatch = 5000;

int rssMiB() {
  final out =
      Process.runSync('ps', ['-o', 'rss=', '-p', '$pid']).stdout as String;
  return int.parse(out.trim()) ~/ 1024;
}

void work(bool usePool) {
  // 4096 UTF-16 code units: too long to be a tagged pointer, so every result
  // is a real heap allocation.
  final base = 'x' * 4096;
  for (var i = 0; i < perBatch; i++) {
    void body() =>
        base.toNSString().stringByAppendingString('$i'.toNSString());
    if (usePool) {
      autoReleasePool(body);
    } else {
      body();
    }
  }
}

void worker((SendPort, bool) arg) {
  final (sendPort, usePool) = arg;
  for (var batch = 1; batch <= batches; batch++) {
    work(usePool);
    sendPort.send('after ${batch * perBatch} calls: rss ${rssMiB()} MiB');
  }
  sendPort.send(null);
}

void main(List<String> args) async {
  final usePool = args.contains('--pool');
  print('pool: $usePool, start: rss ${rssMiB()} MiB');
  final receivePort = ReceivePort();
  await Isolate.spawn(worker, (receivePort.sendPort, usePool));
  await for (final Object? message in receivePort) {
    if (message == null) break;
    print(message);
  }
  receivePort.close();
}

Output (objective_c 9.6.1, arm64 macOS 26.6.2):

pool: false, start: rss 289 MiB       pool: true, start: rss 315 MiB
after  5000 calls: rss 318 MiB        after  5000 calls: rss 300 MiB
after 10000 calls: rss 343 MiB        after 10000 calls: rss 300 MiB
after 15000 calls: rss 368 MiB        after 15000 calls: rss 300 MiB
after 20000 calls: rss 394 MiB        after 20000 calls: rss 300 MiB
after 25000 calls: rss 419 MiB        after 25000 calls: rss 300 MiB
after 30000 calls: rss 444 MiB        after 30000 calls: rss 300 MiB
after 35000 calls: rss 470 MiB        after 35000 calls: rss 300 MiB
after 40000 calls: rss 495 MiB        after 40000 calls: rss 300 MiB

I tried generating a small shim in Objective-C for each method so that objc_autoreleaseReturnValue /
objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue elision triggers and the returned object never enters the pool.

The problem is that some methods (e.g. dataTaskWithRequest:) seem to add objects to the pool as part of their implementations.

So it really seems like, unless we make every call in the context of an explicit autorelease pool (either manually in the client code [I can do this in package:cupertino_http but it is tedious because an autorelease callback can't span an asynchronous gap] or automatically in generated code), the best way to handle this is by creating a new pool every time we handle isolate events. See dart-lang/sdk#61129

issue.title: [objective_c] Use `objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue`
issue.body_html:
objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue will attempt to promote a recently autoreleased value to a strong reference, reducing the number of references in the autorelease pool. If the reference was not recently autoreleased (presumably it checks the top O(1) refs in the pool's stack), this function behaves the same as objc_retain, so it's a safe drop-in replacement.

  • Blocks still have to use objc_retainBlock, since there's no block equivalent of objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue.
  • No FFIgen changes are necessary, since the actual objc_retain calls happen in package:objective_c.
  • For testing, I've removed a bunch of autorelease pools from various ref counting tests, since they're no longer necessary.

Fixes #3653
